newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends firmer in thin, rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends firmer in thin, rangebound trade.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled a thinly-traded session slightly higher as speculative and local buying carried prices over unchanged late in the session, dealers said.
One floor source said the funds tried to hit stops they believed to be around 76.50 in March, but no stops were elected and prices slid off the highs by the close.
March settled up 0.23 cent at 76.53 cents per pound, traded 76.70 to 75.90 cents. The back months closed 0.25 higher to 0.11 cent lower.
Volume was estimated at only 6,500 lots.
Players await the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand report, released Thursday at 0830 EST.
Industry sources expect the USDA to raise its estimate for the U.S. crop slightly, to between 18.6 million bales and 18.788 million 480-lb bales.
The crop was forecast at 18.59 million 480-lb bales in November.
